cards.claim: A scalar is a quantity that has magnitude only.
cards.quote: A scalar quantity is a quantity with magnitude only.

cards.claim: A vector has both magnitude and direction and adds by the triangle law (equivalently the parallelogram law).
cards.quote: A vector quantity is a quantity that has both a magnitude and a direction and obeys the triangle law of addition or equivalently the parallelogram law of addition.

cards.claim: The displacement vector is the straight line from the initial to the final position; it does not depend on the path taken between them.
cards.quote: displacement vector is the straight line joining the initial and final positions and does not depend on the actual path undertaken by the object between the two positions.

cards.claim: Two vectors are equal if and only if they have the same magnitude and the same direction.
cards.quote: Two vectors A and B are said to be equal if, and only if, they have the same magnitude and the same direction.

cards.claim: Equality by parallel shifting applies to free vectors; where the location or line of application matters (localised vectors), shifting a vector is not allowed.
cards.quote: In our study, vectors do not have fixed locations. So displacing a vector parallel to itself leaves the vector unchanged. Such vectors are called free vectors. However, in some physical applications, location or line of application of a vector is important.

cards.claim: Path length equals the magnitude of displacement only when the object does not change direction; otherwise path length is greater.
cards.quote: The two quantities are equal only if the object does not change its direction during the course of motion. In all other cases, the path length is greater than the magnitude of displacement.

cards.claim: For fixed initial and final positions P and Q, three different paths (PABCQ, PDQ, PBEFQ) all give the same displacement vector PQ.
cards.quote: given the initial and final positions as P and Q, the displacement vector is the same PQ for different paths of journey, say PABCQ, PDQ, and PBEFQ.

cards.claim: Treating path length as equal to the magnitude of displacement is wrong in general: displacement depends only on the end points while path length depends on the actual path.
cards.quote: The path length traversed by an object between two points is, in general, not the same as the magnitude of displacement. The displacement depends only on the end points; the path length (as the name implies) depends on the actual path.

cards.claim: NCERT Exercise 3.1 asks the learner to classify ten physical quantities as scalar or vector.
cards.quote: State, for each of the following physical quantities, if it is a scalar or a vector : volume, mass, speed, acceleration, density, number of moles, velocity, angular frequency, displacement, angular velocity.

question.exam: NCERT Class XI Physics Part I textbook exercises
question.paper: Chapter 3 Motion in a Plane, Exercises (Reprint 2026-27)

cards.claim: NCERT answer to 3.1: volume, mass, speed, density, number of moles and angular frequency are scalars; acceleration, velocity, displacement and angular velocity are vectors.
cards.quote: 3.1 Volume, mass, speed, density, number of moles, angular frequency are scalars; the rest are vectors.

cards.claim: NCERT Exercise 3.8 asks for the displacement magnitude of three skaters going from P to the diametrically opposite point Q of a 200 m radius circle, and for which girl it equals the path length.
cards.quote: Three girls skating on a circular ice ground of radius 200 m start from a point P on the edge of the ground and reach a point Q diametrically opposite to P following different paths as shown in Fig. 3.19. What is the magnitude of the displacement vector for each ? For which girl is this equal to the actual length of path skate ?

question.exam: NCERT Class XI Physics Part I textbook exercises
question.paper: Chapter 3 Motion in a Plane, Exercises (Reprint 2026-27)

cards.claim: NCERT answer to 3.8: the displacement is 400 m for each girl, and it equals the path length for girl B.
NCERT Exercise 3.11 compares the average speed and the magnitude of average velocity for a 23 km circuitous cab ride to a hotel 10 km away, taking 28 min.
cards.quote: A passenger arriving in a new town wishes to go from the station to a hotel located 10 km away on a straight road from the station. A dishonest cabman takes him along a circuitous path 23 km long and reaches the hotel in 28 min. What is (a) the average speed of the taxi, (b) the magnitude of average velocity ? Are the two equal ?

question.exam: NCERT Class XI Physics Part I textbook exercises
question.paper: Chapter 3 Motion in a Plane, Exercises (Reprint 2026-27)

cards.claim: NCERT answer to 3.11: average speed 49.3 km/h, magnitude of average velocity 21.4 km/h; they are not equal because they coincide only for a straight path.
cards.quote: 3.11 (a) 49.3 km h–1 ; (b) 21.4 km h–1. No, the average speed equals average velocity magnitude only for a straight path.
